documents.title: NE555 timer notes
documents.text:
# Timing modes

The NE555 timer can generate a single pulse in monostable operation. Astable operation produces a repeating waveform. The timing network uses resistors and a capacitor.

# Reset input

The RESET input overrides timing activity. Pulling RESET low stops the NE555 output. Keep this input at a defined level when reset control is not needed.

documents.title: NE556 dual timer notes
documents.text:
# Two timers

The NE556 contains two timing circuits in one package. Each timer has its own timing connections. It is useful when a design needs two timing functions rather than one NE555 timer.

# Shared supply

The two NE556 timers share power connections. Supply decoupling helps prevent switching activity in one timing circuit from disturbing the other.

documents.title: Resistor fundamentals
documents.text:
# Resistance

A resistor opposes the flow of electric current. Resistance is measured in ohms. Ohm's law relates the voltage across a resistor to its resistance and the current through it.

# Colour bands

Colour bands on an axial resistor encode its resistance and tolerance. Read the band sequence in the correct direction. A multimeter can check the resistance when the part marking is unclear.

documents.title: Capacitor fundamentals
documents.text:
# Charge storage

A capacitor stores energy in an electric field between conductors. Capacitance is measured in farads. A polarised capacitor must be connected with the correct polarity.

# Supply decoupling

A decoupling capacitor supplies brief local current demands and reduces disturbances on a power rail. It belongs near the circuit it supports, with a short connection to the supply and return.

documents.title: Diodes and inductive loads
documents.text:
# Direction of conduction

A diode conducts primarily in one direction. Its terminals are the anode and cathode. A stripe commonly identifies the cathode on an axial diode package.

# Flyback protection

Interrupting current through a relay coil can produce a voltage spike. A flyback diode across a DC coil provides a path for the stored inductive current when the driver switches off.

documents.title: LED connection notes
documents.text:
# Current limiting

An LED needs a controlled forward current. A series resistor is a simple way to limit current from a voltage supply. Connecting the light-emitting diode directly to an unsuitable voltage source can damage it.

# Polarity

An LED has an anode and cathode. Check its package markings or datasheet before assembly. Reversing the LED can prevent illumination.

documents.title: Push-button inputs
documents.text:
# Contact bounce

Mechanical switch contacts can open and close repeatedly during one press. This contact bounce can make a digital input report several transitions for a single button action.

# Debouncing

Software debouncing accepts a new button state only after it remains stable for an interval. Hardware filtering and a Schmitt-trigger input are other ways to obtain a clean transition.

documents.title: PCB power and return paths
documents.text:
# Return paths

Current must return to its source. A long, narrow shared return path can couple switching noise into sensitive circuitry. Place components and route connections to keep important current loops short.

# Local capacitors

Place a supply decoupling capacitor close to an integrated circuit. Short supply and return connections reduce the loop area. A distant capacitor can be less effective at supporting fast local current changes.

documents.title: Soldering inspection
documents.text:
# Solder bridges

Excess solder can join neighbouring pads that should remain separate. Inspect fine-pitch leads for unintended bridges. Continuity checks help confirm whether adjacent electrical nets have become connected.

# Rework

Flux and solder wick can help remove excess solder. Reinspect the pads and connections after rework. Repeated heating can damage pads or nearby components.

documents.title: Railway curve planning
documents.text:
# Curve radius

A curve that is too tight for a locomotive or carriage can cause derailments or coupling problems. Choose a radius compatible with the rolling stock. Test the longest vehicles on the tightest planned bend.

# Transitions

A transition introduces curvature gradually between a straight and a curve. Avoid abrupt reverse bends with long vehicles. A short straight between opposing curves can reduce coupling stress.

documents.title: Turnout operation
documents.text:
# Route selection

A turnout directs a train onto one of two routes. Its position determines which branch is connected to the approaching track. Check the selected route before sending a train through the junction.

# Point rails

The movable point rails must close correctly against the stock rails. Dirt or mechanical obstruction can prevent full closure and cause a wheel to take the wrong path.

documents.title: Track gauge and model scale
documents.text:
# Gauge

Track gauge is the distance between the inner faces of the two running rails. Wheelsets and track must use compatible geometry. Incorrect gauge can cause poor running or derailments.

# Scale

Model scale describes the ratio between a model and the full-size object. Scale and track gauge describe different measurements. Two models can use the same track gauge while representing different prototype scales.

documents.title: DCC locomotive control
documents.text:
# Addresses

Digital Command Control sends commands through the track. A locomotive decoder responds to its configured address, allowing independently addressed locomotives to share a powered track.

# Decoder

A decoder interprets digital commands and controls outputs such as the motor and lights. Check compatibility between the decoder, locomotive motor and installation space before fitting it.

documents.title: Railway occupancy detection
documents.text:
# Current sensing

A current-sensing detector reports a track section as occupied when rolling stock draws current from that section. An unlit wagon without a detectable electrical load may not trigger this kind of detector.

# Optical sensing

An optical detector can detect a train when it interrupts a beam of light. Sensor placement and ambient light affect detection. This method does not require the vehicle to draw track power.

documents.title: Signals and route protection
documents.text:
# Block protection

A block signal indicates whether a train may enter the next protected section. Occupancy detection can inform the signal state. An occupied block should not be presented as clear for another train.

# Interlocking

Interlocking prevents conflicting routes from being set simultaneously. It coordinates turnout positions and signals so that incompatible train movements are not authorised together.

documents.title: Rolling-stock clearances
documents.text:
# Swept envelope

A long carriage overhangs the track centreline on a curve. Check its swept envelope beside platforms, tunnel walls and neighbouring tracks. Static measurements on a straight track do not capture this movement.

# Bridges

Check both height and width beneath a bridge. Account for the tallest vehicles and any overhead equipment. Verify clearance on the actual track alignment rather than using the bridge opening alone.

documents.title: Notas sobre via C
documents.text:
# Balastro integrado

A via C tem uma base que representa o balastro e suporta os carris. O leito integrado facilita a montagem de um traçado temporário sobre uma superfície plana.

# Uniões

As uniões entre peças devem ficar bem encaixadas. Uma ligação mecânica incompleta pode deixar os carris desalinhados ou provocar mau contacto eléctrico.

documents.title: Limpeza de rodas e carris
documents.text:
# Rodas

Gordura e sujidade nas rodas prejudicam a captação de corrente da locomotiva. Limpar as superfícies de contacto ajuda a evitar paragens intermitentes. Use um método compatível com os materiais do veículo.

# Carris

Uma camada de sujidade ou oxidação nos carris pode interromper o contacto eléctrico. Inspeccione e limpe a superfície de rolamento. Evite produtos que deixem resíduos isolantes.
